guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.title: Wedding Contact Sheets: Review Hundreds of Photos Fast
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.desc: Use a contact sheet to shortlist wedding photos with clients or family, with sensible grid sizes, labels and a workflow that avoids version chaos.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.lead: A contact sheet is a decision tool. Include a file name or number under every frame, or nobody can tell you which images they mean.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.f1v: 4 × 5 or 5 × 6 per page keeps thumbnails readable
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.f2v: Print the file name or a sequential number under each frame
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.f3v: PDF for markup and sharing; JPEG for a quick preview
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.f4v: Split by part of the day, not into one huge document
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.s1: Sort by scene first — preparation, ceremony, portraits, reception — then generate one sheet per scene. Consistent numbering is more important than a beautiful layout: the reviewer should be able to circle 'C-042' and have you find it instantly. Export as a PDF so it can be annotated on a tablet, and keep a mapping from sheet numbers back to original file names.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.s2: US and European photographers commonly deliver a proofing gallery online, but a printable contact sheet is still useful for families choosing album images together, and for any situation where internet access is unreliable. If you are working across languages, use numbers and a short scene code rather than descriptive captions that need translating. Check that the PDF embeds the fonts used in its labels.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.s3: Avoid a grid so dense that expressions are invisible, and do not apply a heavy watermark across the middle of faces. Keep the source images unmodified and note which round of review each sheet represents — the fastest way to lose a selection is to have three sheets all labelled 'final'. Once choices are locked, record them in one list, not in scattered messages.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.q1: How many photos per contact sheet page?
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.a1: Twenty to thirty. Smaller grids make expressions and focus easier to judge.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.q2: Should I use numbers or file names?
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.a2: Short sequential numbers are easiest to discuss aloud; keep a lookup table mapping them to the original file names.
guides.wedding-photo-contact-sheet.a3: PDF for anything that will be annotated, printed or shared across devices. A JPEG is fine for a quick single-screen preview.
